id.description: Stable while the condition holds: kind and subject.

since.description: When the condition began or will begin, where known (server time).

expires_at.description: Valid through the end of this date.

secret.description: Shown this once - it cannot be read again.

active.description: Update only; false revokes the key at once.

role.description: Create only: copy this role's grants (no grant fields then).

changes.description: For a change, each field as {from, to}; for a create or delete, the whole record. Never a secret.

retention.description: The log keeps this many entries (QUERYAPIGATE_AUDIT_LOG_LIMIT).

meta.description: name, version, connection, format and page, when known.

keys.description: API keys whose collections grant names it.

database.description: The database name, or the file path for SQLite/DuckDB/H2.

options.description: Driver options passed through to the connection (sslmode, jdbc_url, ...).

password.description: Masked as ******** unless it is a ${ENV_VAR} reference; send the mask back (or leave password out) to keep it.

key_secrets.description: The new example keys' secrets - shown this once.

keys_still_granted.description: Other keys granted an example collection; that grant is now inert.

partial.description: Some are: an interrupted load (POST again completes it).

collections.description: Every query in these collections, including ones filed there later.

connections.description: "*" for every connection, or a list of names (ad-hoc SQL and every saved query on them).

queries.description: Saved queries runnable by name, independent of connections; an object entry can allow writes through that one query.

code.description: A failed run's error code (API.md, Errors), from 0.13 on.

kind.description: A saved query run, or ad-hoc SQL (/execute_sql, /execute_mongo, MCP execute_sql).

params.description: Ad-hoc only: the parameters' names - never their values.

query.description: The saved query; null for ad-hoc SQL.

sql.description: Ad-hoc only, unless QUERYAPIGATE_HISTORY_ADHOC_SQL says 'hash' or 'none'; at most 4000 characters (sql_truncated).

transport.description: The front door it came through.

next_cursor.description: Pass as ?cursor= for the next page; null on the last.

default.description: Present only when the parameter has a default.

from_claim.description: Bound from the signed-in caller's token claim.

error.description: Why it could not be analyzed.

on.description: The join condition; empty if none.

cache_ttl.description: The published version's (or newest draft's) response cache TTL, in seconds.

created_at.description: When its first version was saved.

description.description: The published version's, or the newest draft's.

endpoint.description: Where the published version is served, e.g. /q/name.

last_used_at.description: Its newest stored run, of any version; null if it never ran.

placeholders.description: Every parameter the query uses, in order of first use.

run_count.description: Runs of this version stored in history - in a query's detail only.

status.description: published: served now; draft: never served (newer than the published version, or nothing is published); previous: served once, still runnable with ?version=

author.description: Defaults to the calling key's name.

publish.description: Publish the new version at once instead of keeping it as a draft.

env_value.description: The raw value, for a .env export; null at the default and always for a secret.

experimental.description: A setting of an experimental feature (outside the compatibility promise).

value.description: The effective value; a secret only as "configured" or "enabled".

code.description: Stable and machine-readable, e.g. query_not_found, param_invalid, table_not_allowed, rate_limited - every code is listed in API.md under Errors.

detail.description: The database driver's own message, where there is one.

error.description: Human-readable; wording may change between releases.

errors.description: Per-parameter problems, when the parameter rules were invalid.

request_id.description: Matches the X-Request-Id header and the server log.

timeout.description: The time limit that was exceeded, when query_timeout.

info.description: Run SQL against configured databases and get the results back over HTTP.

get.description: Not just what /openapi.json already documents (parameters, description, connection) but the governance half it has no field for: whether a response can be cached and for how long, whether this specific caller can write through this query (may differ per query - see per-query write curation under Authentication and permissions), and this caller's own rate limit alongside the server-wide one. Scoped the same way /openapi.json already scopes its saved-query list - a query this caller cannot reach through /q/<name> is never listed here either. Requires authentication like any other functional endpoint (unlike /openapi.json, this is never public), since the whole point is answering "what can *I* use."

rate_limit.description: This caller's own additional limit, e.g. "100/minute", or null when it has none of its own.

server_rate_limit.description: QUERYAPIGATE_RATE_LIMIT, checked in addition to rate_limit above, or null when the server has no limit configured.

cache_ttl.description: Seconds a response may be served from cache, or null when uncached.

can_write.description: Whether this caller specifically can write through this query.
